component.name: Natter
component.summary: Unofficial WhatsApp client that fits your desktop

description.p: Natter shows WhatsApp Web in a native GTK and libadwaita window and connects it to the rest of your desktop: notifications, the tray, the dock and the keyboard.
Natter is unofficial. It isn’t made by, endorsed by or affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. It runs the real WhatsApp Web, the same way your browser would, and you link it to your phone the same way.

ul.li: One notification per chat, with the sender’s picture; clicking it opens that chat
Quiet hours, and an unread count in the tray and on the dock icon
Ctrl+K jumps to any chat by name, or messages a phone number you haven’t saved
Paste or drop pictures and files into a chat, or send them from the file manager
wa.me and whatsapp:// links open in Natter
A privacy blur that hides names, pictures and messages until you point at them
Several accounts, each with its own session
Keeps running in the background, and gives memory back while its window is closed

description.p: Voice and video calls open in your web browser: they need WebRTC, which the WebKit that Natter is built on doesn’t offer.
First release as io.github.Officialbabs.Natter, with a Flatpak, and support for GNOME, KDE Plasma, Xfce, Sway and Ada.
